correctness.rationale: Every graph edge changes one and only one level-threshold or dimer coordinate. Removing source-only dimers, changing remaining monomers, then installing target-only dimers achieves exactly the L1 lower bound. For k=2r, complementary low and normal high thresholds alternate with mutually exclusive one-bits, while active dimer boundaries force adjacent low bits to zero, hence the image lies in a Fibonacci cube of precisely kn-1 bits. Each coordinate has an independent edge representative, and Θ-classes force >=kn-1 Hamming coordinates. The standalone checker exhaustively reproduced pairwise distances and bit constraints on specified finite instances, without being mistaken for universal proof.

value.rationale: The originating authors explicitly posed reducing their Fibonacci host dimension as Problem 5.10. The even-k all-n theorem reduces their bound by (k-2)n and additionally proves exact minimality in the isometric setting; the proof supplies a constructive shortest-path algorithm and an optimal metric labeling. These are nontrivial graph-network invariants, not a routine evaluation of a published counting table.
